findings.title: Pending-finish and after-turn checkpoints lose active model and replacement context
tests: V3-A runtime model and replacement context survive response pause
V3-A runtime model and replacement context survive finish pause
findings.actual: prepareRequest returns selected-runtime-model plus compacted-context. Both no-pause controls call that model twice with compacted context. JSON pause/restore during response or finish produces second call to constructor model synthetic with original-context instead. Response-pause also passes original-context to the pending finish callback.
findings.impact: A resumed request can use the wrong model and restore context removed or replaced by preparation, despite callback counts being correct. Public PrepareRequest permits replacement runtime context/model; the uninterrupted controls prove its current behavior.
findings.cause: The request phase stores runtime data, but message_end/recordPendingFinish/recordTurnCompletion replace it with assistant index and booleans. ResumePendingFinish and ResumeAfterTurn reconstruct from Agent public state and fresh createLoopConfig, not the active loop context/config.
findings.suggestion: Persist active model, reasoning, exact runtime context and stable tool binding through every continuation phase, including pendingFinish and afterTurn. Restore the pending callback/next-turn transition from that runtime snapshot while preserving the public transcript separately.

findings.title: Resuming a tool batch re-enables a tool excluded from that request
tests: V3-B restored tool batch retains per-request restricted tool loadout
findings.actual: Initial registry contains allowed and excluded; prepareRequest restricts context.tools to allowed. Original assistant calls allowed then excluded. No-pause control executes only allowed and produces isError=true for excluded. Pausing after allowed, serializing to JSON and restoring executes excluded too, giving effects=[allowed,excluded] and isError=false.
findings.impact: Pause/restore broadens the executable tool set for a previously issued batch and can run an effect that the original request would reject.
findings.cause: The tools continuation preserves completion IDs but not that turn's effective tool set. resumePaused uses createContextSnapshot() from all public state tools, and runAgentLoopResumeTools executes against it.
findings.suggestion: Bind each pending tool batch to its original effective tool declarations and resolvable implementations, restore only that set, and fail closed if the exact binding is unavailable. Do not substitute the full current Agent registry.
